references.text: The Lord promises Abraham that he will become the father of many nations, and Abraham believes the promise, establishing the prophetic vision of a future that Jesus refers to as his own day.
Abraham's willingness to sacrifice his son on Mount Moriah demonstrates deep faith in God's promises of future salvation, a moment when he looks forward to the day Jesus describes.
John presents Jesus as the Word who became flesh, the same day Abraham saw in faith, now revealed in history.
Paul explains that Abraham believed God, and it was credited to him as righteousness, and that those who believe are Abraham's children, sharing in the promise of the day Jesus came.
